text:
sanjay: Quick ask — prepping for tomorrow's account kickoff with Helix. Need a short customer-facing checklist (6–8 lines) about caching / batching / streaming best-practices we can paste into the invite, plus a tiny config snippet for their engineers. Also: what immediate signals should we flag as renewal risk?

maria_cs: Copyable blurb you can paste into the invite:
• Keep a small warm pool: pre-warm 2–3 representative requests after deploys to avoid cold-token latency spikes.
• Use prefix caching for stable prompts (e.g., welcome flows) to cut downstream token spend.
• Batch where user-level latency tolerance allows (batch size 4–8 typical).
• Stream for interactive UIs; fall back to non-streaming for critical logs / billing accuracy.
• Monitor p50/p95 latency plus tokens per request — sudden drops in tokens/day can indicate adoption risk.
• Capture feedback in-product (thumbs / tiny post-response survey) and sync weekly.

devon_se: Tiny config example engineers can drop in (adjust values for their traffic):
```yaml
inference: 
  warm_pool_size: 3
  batch: 
    max_batch_size: 8
    max_latency_ms: 50
  streaming: true
  prefix_cache_ttl_seconds: 3600
```

lucy_oncall: Renewal-risk watchlist (quick):
• Persistent p95 latency > 500ms for >1 hour
• Tokens-per-day down >40% week-over-week
• Repeated 5xx errors or increased queue depth
• Spike in negative feedback flags or churned seats

maria_cs: Also add a tiny troubleshooting line for CS: "If customer reports cold starts, verify warm_pool_size and check recent deploys; if warm_pool is set and p95 still high, ask eng to confirm KV cache warming ran."

devon_se: Extra tip: recommend a staged rollout to Helix with canary traffic at 5% for 24h, verify prefix cache hit-rate > 60% before 100% cutover.

reminder-bot: Reminder created: follow up with Helix in 48 hours to capture initial feedback and adoption signal. :bell:

sanjay: perfect, thanks all — I'll paste this into the invite and add the follow-up.
